rejected.label: [0] uniswap-pools (3 pools, 0.003 HBAR)
rejected.because: Returns only {id, protocol, tvlUSD}. Even if Uniswap pools include ETH pairs, tvlUSD alone doesn't provide token reserves or pair price; you cannot derive current ETH price reliably from tvlUSD.

rejected.label: [1] curve-pools (3 pools, 0.006 HBAR)
rejected.because: Curve stableswap pools are focused on stablecoins and return only tvlUSD. They generally don't provide an ETH price signal and the response shape lacks reserves/prices, so useless for ETH price.

rejected.label: [2] dex-pools (3 pools, 0.009 HBAR)
rejected.because: Although broader (multiple DEXes), this also only returns tvlUSD per pool. Breadth doesn't help because the required fields (token reserves or price) are missing.

rejected.label: [3] uniswap-pools (10 pools, 0.01 HBAR)
rejected.because: Same data limitations as option 0; buying more Uniswap pools doesn't help because none of the responses include reserves or token price.

rejected.label: [4] curve-pools (10 pools, 0.02 HBAR)
rejected.because: Same as option 1 and expensive; Curve stableswap tvl data won't produce ETH price and is the most costly of the set.

events.reasoning: None of the available on-chain data products actually return token prices or pool reserves — they only return pool IDs and tvlUSD. That data is insufficient to compute a live ETH price. Therefore it's correct to buy nothing from these options and instead use a price feed / oracle or a data source that returns token prices or pair reserves.
